Here is a comprehensive summary of the codebase. --- ## Framework: Next.js (App Router) **Version:** `next@^16.3.1-canary.3` (canary build of Next.js 16) **React:** `react@19.1.0` / `react-dom@19.1.0` **Tooling:** TypeScript 5, Vitest for testing, Vite plugins for TS path resolution --- ## Routing Convention: App Router (`app/` directory) This project uses the **App Router** (not the older Pages Router). There is no `pages/` directory. The routing is file-system-based from the `app/` directory: | File | Route | Role | |---|---|---| | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | Root layout | Wraps all pages; defines `` and ``; exports `metadata` for the `` title | | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | `/` (homepage) | The single page component, renders "User Preferences" placeholder | There are no nested routes, route groups, dynamic routes, or API routes present. --- ## Component Conventions ### Layout (`app/layout.tsx`) - **Server Component by default** (no `"use client"` directive). - Exports a `RootLayout` component accepting `{ children: React.ReactNode }`. - Exports `metadata: Metadata` for SEO/page title (`"Theme Settings"`). - Simple structure: `{children}`. ### Page (`app/page.tsx`) - **Server Component by default** (no `"use client"` directive). - Exports a default function `Home()`. - Currently a simple placeholder rendering an `

` and `

` tag. ### Key conventions observed: - **All components are server components by default** -- there are zero `"use client"` or `"use server"` directives anywhere in the codebase. - No `async` functions are used on the page or layout yet. - No data fetching (`fetch`, `cookies()`, `headers()`) is used yet. - No imports from `next/headers` or `next/cookies` exist yet. --- ## Cookies, Headers, and Server Components - **No cookie or header usage is currently implemented.** No imports from `next/headers`, no calls to `cookies()` or `headers()`, and no `"use server"` directives. - The pattern the project is set up to follow would be the standard Next.js 16 App Router conventions: - `import { cookies } from "next/headers"` in a Server Component or Route Handler to read/write cookies. - `import { headers } from "next/headers"` for reading request headers. - Both are async in Next.js 16 and require `await`. --- ## Project Structure Overview ``` /workspace/ .git/ # Git repository (initial commit or just initialized) .gitignore # Ignores node_modules/ and __agent_eval__/ app/ layout.tsx # Root layout (server component, Metadata export) page.tsx # Home page route "/" (server component) __agent_eval__/ # Evaluation harness (gitignored) run.mjs # 10 KB eval runner script next.config.ts # Minimal Next.js config (empty NextConfig object) tsconfig.json # TypeScript config with @/* path alias -> ./* root package.json # Dependencies and scripts package-lock.json node_modules/ opencode.json # OpenCode AI configuration (provider + permissions) ``` ### TSConfig Highlights - **Path alias:** `@/*` maps to the project root (`./*`), so imports like `@/app/page` would resolve. - **Module resolution:** `bundler` (modern). - **Strict mode:** enabled. ### Package.json Scripts -
